# Evaluation report (generated by `python -m research.evaluate`)

**Dataset:** 82,486 unique emails from 6 public corpora (42,891 spam/phishing, 39,595 legitimate).

**Split:** 65,988 train / 16,498 test, stratified, seed 42.

## Held-out test set

| Model | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | False-positive rate | Train time |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Complement Naive Bayes | 97.26% | 99.09% | 95.61% | 97.32% | 0.95% | 0.0 s |
| Logistic Regression (balanced) | 98.62% | 98.64% | 98.72% | 98.68% | 1.48% | 1.2 s |
| Linear SVM (balanced) | 99.13% | 99.15% | 99.18% | 99.17% | 0.92% | 17.0 s |

Linear SVM confusion matrix: TN=7,846 · FP=73 · FN=70 · TP=8,509

## Inference latency

Median **1.31 ms**, p95 6.21 ms per message over 1000 messages (single-threaded CPU, cleaning + TF-IDF + SVM + confidence, no LLM call).

## Leave-one-corpus-out (train on 5 corpora, test on the unseen 6th)

| Unseen corpus | Emails | Accuracy | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| CEAS_08 | 39,154 | 83.2% | 83.86% |
| Enron | 29,767 | 80.97% | 81.23% |
| Ling | 2,859 | 90.66% | 75.88% |
| Nazario | 1,565 | 53.23% | 69.47% |
| Nigerian_Fraud | 3,332 | 99.01% | 99.5% |
| SpamAssasin | 5,809 | 90.88% | 85.68% |

Scores on an unseen corpus are lower than on the random split: emails from the same corpus share vocabulary and formatting, so the random split is the optimistic case.
